messages.content: You are a creative storyteller. Write vivid prose with strong imagery.
Write a 200-word short story about a lighthouse keeper who finds a message in a bottle from herself.

message.content:
The sea threw it against the rocks at half past three, when the Atlantic wind was screaming and the lamp above her would not stop turning. Maren pulled on her wool coat and climbed down the slick iron stairs, salt stinging her lips.

The bottle was green, thick, sea-worn—and inside, a slip of paper folded twice.

She unfolded it with numb fingers and recognized her own handwriting instantly. The same cramped slant, the same cross through the final *n*.

*You will be asked to leave the lighthouse on March 14th. Do not.*

Her breath caught. The date was tomorrow.

She read it again, then a third time, searching for some prank, some explanation. There was no explanation. Only the words, only her hand, only the faint impression of a wax seal she did not remember pressing.

The lamp above her turned, slow and eternal, casting its white arm across the water.

Maren walked back up the spiral stairs, the bottle dangling from her wrist. She would not sleep tonight. She would not leave. And when morning came, she would write another note, fold it twice, seal it with wax, and carry it down to the rocks before the tide turned.

She would throw it out to sea, and wait.
